chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Junub (one with major sexual impurity) sitting in the mosques. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he may pass through all of them, except for the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: One in a state of major ritual impurity (Junub)
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (in Medina)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in a state of Junub sit in the mosque?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between sitting and passing through for a Junub, a ruling derived from the general principle of ritual purity in sacred spaces. Notably, it excludes Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Nabi from the permission to pass through, reflecting their elevated status as the primary sanctuaries where even transit is restricted for the impure, a view supported by Shia jurists who emphasize the specific holiness of these two mosques over others.
